sentences.text: Gyposaurus means "vulture lizard" and refers to a basal sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic of South Africa.
Robert Broom named Gyposaurus capensis in 1911 based on a partial skeleton found in the Upper Elliot Formation of Orange Free State, initially placing it in the genus Hortalotarsus.
A separate species, Gyposaurus sinensis, was named in 1941 by Yang Zhongjian using four specimens from the Early Jurassic Lufeng Formation of Yunnan Province, China.
Michael Cooper synonymized Gyposaurus capensis with Massospondylus in 1981, a classification that has been generally accepted.
Galton referred Gyposaurus sinensis to Lufengosaurus in 1976, while Dong Zhiming referred it to Anchisaurus in 1992.
The parent group of Gyposaurus is Anchisauridae.
Gyposaurus lived approximately 195 million years ago during the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian) in what is now Africa and Asia.
The animal lived from the Hettangian to the Toarcian stages, between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago.
It is debated whether Gyposaurus sinensis is a valid species or a junior synonym of Lufengosaurus huenei, as some referred specimens require further study.
